en: Magellan was killed by the warriors of Lapu-Lapu during the Battle of Mactan, not in a one-on-one duel.
Marcela Agoncillo and her daughters actually sewed the first official Philippine flag based on Emilio Aguinaldo's design.
Jose Rizal did not lead the armed revolution; Andres Bonifacio founded the Katipunan to lead the armed struggle.
The three stars on the Philippine flag represent the three principal island groups: Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao.
The United States did not formally recognize Philippine independence until July 4, 1946, decades after the 1898 declaration.
The Philippine eagle is the national bird, but it is endemic only to the forests of Luzon, Samar, Leyte, and Mindanao.
The sampaguita is the official national flower of the Philippines, not the rare waling-waling orchid.
Fe del Mundo was the first woman admitted to Harvard Medical School, breaking the institution's gender barrier in 1936.
The Barong Tagalog is made of translucent piña fabric and worn untucked to historically prove the wearer carried no hidden weapons.
Only the Congress of the Philippines can declare the existence of a state of war, even though the President is Commander-in-Chief.
The Sinulog festival in Cebu honors the Santo Niño, celebrating the Catholic faith rather than the arrival of Ferdinand Magellan.
The Aeta people are among the earliest inhabitants of the Philippines, traditionally residing in mountainous and forested regions rather than coastal areas.
